There is and There are in Questions
We use “there is” and “there are” to say that something exists. We use “there is” and “there are” when we first refer to the existence or presence of someone or something.

How to use there is and there are:

  • We use “there is” for singular and “there are” for plural.
  • Use “there is” with uncountable nouns.
  • The contraction of “there is” is there's. In informal contexts, you can contract there are as there're.

Questions with There is and There are

To form a question, we have to place is or are before “there” which means that we use the verb to be first and there right after it.

For example:
Is there a new manager in the company?
Are there any programs to design facades?
Please tell us about CASE; are there any key features?
Is there a particular moment when it emerged?
Are there any other features or precise information you think that's relevant to mention?
Infinitive to Talk about Unexpected Events with Only
The infinitive is the base form of a verb and we use it to express the purpose of something or someone's opinion or feeling about something.

How to use only with infinitives:

  • Sometimes only is used before the infinitive.
  • Use only to emphasize on the limitations or particularities of the action.
  • Only focuses on the specific purpose of the action.

Examples:
  • We need to use this new software only to design architectural models and constructions.
  • The software designers are creating new programs only to gain more reputation in the market.
Sometimes companies need to adopt methodologies and tools only to meet their specific requirements.
We have integration and trends, in which a typical CASE environment integrates a variety of tools only to facilitate the flow of software development and data transferring.

Interviewer: Welcome to our daily show. Today, we have a special guest only to talk to our audience about CASE. Our guest is the CEO at a computer software multinational.
Guest: Thank you for the invitation.
Interviewer: Please tell us about CASE. Are there any key features? Is there a particular time for its development?

Guest: Well, CASE stands for Computer-aided software engineering. It started as a project in 1968 at Michigan University. CASE is the domain of software tools used to design and implement applications and operating system software. CASE inspiration came from the computer-aided design CAD tools used to design hardware products. CASE tools serve to develop high-quality, defect-free software, and maintainable only to develop and guarantee software with quality.
Interviewer: Are there any other features or precise information do you consider relevant to mention?
Guest: Absolutely, some other features are the design tools like flowchart or pseudocodes. These tools can work when a program and its implementation is underway. CASE tools can help the programmers maintain consistency only to provide a list of affected components. And also, we have integration and trends, in which a typical CASE environment integrates a variety of tools only to facilitate the flow of software development and data transferring.

Interviewer: What about the risk factors related to CASE?
Guest: Some significant risk factors for companies implementing CASE technology include inadequate standardization. Sometimes companies need to adopt methodologies and tools only to meet their specific requirements. Also, inadequate training represents a risk because CASE requires time to train people in how to use the tools. Finally, CASE offers capabilities to utilize new types of tools in innovative ways, but without the guidance processes and controls, these new capabilities can cause new problems.
Interviewer: We're running out of time, but thank you for joining us today.
